_placedBy: Four states, not a boolean. 'agent' = a scheduled run placed the order itself, from its own analysis, with nobody asking. 'directed' = an agent placed it because a human asked for it in the moment - machine-executed, human-initiated. 'assisted' = a human executed it with the agent advising - human-executed, machine-informed. 'hand' = a human acting alone. ONLY 'agent' counts toward autonomy. The brokerage reports placed_agent='agentic' for both 'agent' and 'directed' and cannot distinguish them, because the difference is who decided rather than who pressed the button - so the retro must establish whether a published specification and a scheduled run stand behind the order, and file it 'directed' when they do not. Reading the broker's flag alone would count a trade the operator asked for as evidence the system runs unattended, which is the claim the whole board rests on.

Reconciled against the brokerage: 4.54 settled cash plus 121.52 unsettled UPST proceeds, no fees on either leg. Account is flat.

CARRIED BACK, not read from an 8/6 snapshot, and the derivation is stated so the one soft link is visible. This connector exposes no portfolio-history endpoint, so no broker total for the 8/6 close can be fetched. What can be: the account is flat today with 109.88 total and nothing unsettled, the broker returns zero equity orders and zero option orders dated 8/7, and pending deposits are zero - so nothing moved between the 8/6 close and this read. Six connected 8/6 runs each reported 11.98 settled, and the 98.00 sale settled 8/7, which puts the 8/6 close at 11.98 + 98.00 less fees. The only open question is whether the 0.10 of option regulatory fee was booked at trade time or at settlement - 109.88 if at trade time, 109.98 if at settlement. The 8/4 AMD precedent already in this ledger settles it: the broker showed 99.94 unsettled against a 100.00 sale the same day, so fees net out of proceeds at trade time on this account. Hence 109.88. The residual uncertainty is 0.10 and it is named rather than buried.

Read directly from the brokerage after the close: total 109.88, cash 109.88, buying power 109.88, zero equity positions, zero option positions, nothing unsettled. No order of any kind was placed on 8/7, so the session moved no money and the flat line against 8/6 is the account genuinely doing nothing rather than a value repeated for want of a source.

Read from the brokerage at 16:33 ET after the close: total 1007.98, cash 919.58, one equity position marked at 88.40, zero option positions, nothing unsettled, no pending deposits. This is the first point on this curve whose value depends on a MARK rather than on cash alone, so the mark is named rather than buried: 88.40 is 2 OKLO at 44.20, the last extended-hours print, because the official 8/10 close is unpublished at this hour - the broker's close endpoint still returns 8/7 for every symbol and no 8/10 daily bar exists yet. The regular-session last trade was 44.49, which would put the total at 1008.56 instead. What is recorded is the brokerage's own total rather than either reconstruction, and the residual uncertainty is about 0.58 and is stated here rather than left implicit. THE STEP FROM 109.88 IS A DEPOSIT AND NOT TRADING, and the arithmetic closes exactly from three directions: 109.88 plus an operator deposit of 900.00 credited between 09:46 and 10:22 is 1009.88; less the 90.30 paid for 2 OKLO at 45.1499 leaves the 919.58 of settled cash the broker reports; and 919.58 plus the 88.40 mark is 1007.98, the 1.90 of difference from 1009.88 being the unrealized loss on the position and nothing else. The broker returns exactly one order in this account since 8/7 and it is that purchase.

_forced: The 2026-08-05 daily entry mandate obliges the open run to publish a specification every trading day and to mark it 'forced' when a checklist item failed, so that patience and compulsion are measured apart instead of averaged together. A closed trade joins an arm only by way of the specification it came from. All three trades on the board came from no specification at all, so all three sit outside both arms and the arms are empty - which is the honest reading, not a missing number. The reason has now been different on each of four days, and the differences are the useful part: on 8/5 nothing had been published, on 8/6 the first specification published under the mandate went unexecuted and expired, on 8/7 the mandate went undischarged because the open slot fired 143 minutes late and stopped at the staleness guard, and on 8/10 the mandate was discharged, the specification again went unexecuted and expired, and the position the account actually holds came from no specification at all. The mandate was committed 2026-08-05 11:34 ET, after that day's open run had already fired, so its first binding open slot was 2026-08-06.

Correction: the five blind firings previously recorded here were setup tests, not live scheduled runs, and have been removed from run health. No scheduled run has operated yet.

The scheduled runs started recording themselves, and every one of them fired in the small hours rather than in its window - the trigger is a desktop task that runs on next app launch, not a server. Three market-hours slots correctly stopped on the staleness guard and wrote no specification. The retro took two attempts: the 00:45 firing stopped at the scope preflight with the mandate unset, which is the intended safe default rather than a fault, and the 00:58 firing completed once the operator set it. Lateness costs a retro nothing, because it grades a session that has already settled.

Reconciled against the API rather than the log. Both AMD legs confirmed by the broker: bought at 0.71 at 11:56:56 ET, sold at 1.00 at 13:04:44 ET, held 1h 08m, and the account total of 128.90 matches. One gap found - the broker reports unsettled proceeds of 99.94 against the 100.00 on the board, the same 0.06 regulatory fee already carried in the equity curve. state.json belongs to the trading runs, so the retro flags it here instead of editing it.

Attribution left alone but worth stating: the round trip is booked assisted, yet the entry was placed by hand before the mandate with no agent input and only the exit was agent-advised. One row cannot split the two. It stays as booked rather than being quietly re-scored by the run that benefits from the answer; agentTrades remains 0, which is the number the autonomy claim actually rests on.

Drift check: docs/RULES.md is unchanged since it was written, and no exit, sizing, or checklist rule has loosened. The one measurement change - dropping five test firings out of run health - is graded in why.json as PASS on method with a flag on direction, because it moved a published number the favourable way the day after a win. That is the fourth-loosening pattern the rulebook says to name out loud, so it is named.

Both UPST legs confirmed against the API, and the account is FLAT. Bought 4 shares at 31.0899 on a 31.30 limit at 13:34:59 ET; sold 4 shares at 30.3801 on a 30.20 limit at 15:38:23 ET. No fees on either leg. P/L -2.84, -2.28%, held 2h 03m. The arithmetic closes exactly from three directions: 128.90 minus the 124.36 buy leaves the 4.54 the board carried as deployable all afternoon, the 121.52 sale proceeds sit unsettled until 8/6, 4.54 plus 121.52 is the 126.06 total the broker reports, and the broker's own realized-P/L endpoint independently returns -2.84 on one closing trade. Nothing here is reconstructed from P/L arithmetic.

Both UPST legs are filed 'directed', and the test was applied rather than the broker flag read. The broker reports placed_agent='agentic' on both, which it would also report for a genuinely unattended order, so it settles nothing. Filing either as 'agent' needs a published specification in why.json matching instrument, side and limit, and a scheduled run row lining up with it. why.json contains no order specification at all - not for these fills, not for anything, on any date. Neither leg clears the first test, so neither clears the bar. agentTrades stays 0 and the autonomy claim is unchanged by a day on which the account traded.

THE GAP: neither UPST leg has any reasoning entry behind it. This is not a run whose reasoning was thin - it is an order that arrived with none, twice. The buy landed at 13:34:59 ET, twelve minutes after the 13:22 hourly read the book flat, and the 14:21 run found it already open. The record is left showing exactly that. No 'did' entry has been appended to make either fill look decided, no reason has been invented for either, and the trade is carried UNGRADED in the table rather than being given a grade the log cannot support. The position existed, it is recorded, and no published reasoning stands behind it.

The sell contradicts the last thing the board published, and the sequence matters. The pre-close run read the account at 15:37 ET, decided the hold deliberately, and wrote 'Holding 4 UPST overnight' into why.json with its levels and its reasons. The sell filled at 15:38:23 ET - 84 seconds after that read. The run then committed at 15:40:50 ET, about two and a half minutes after the fill, without re-reading the account, so the site went live announcing an overnight hold of a position that no longer existed. The reasoning was sound when it was written and is graded on that basis; what failed is the gap between the read and the push. state.json and moves.json belong to the trading runs, so the retro flags this rather than editing it: state.json still shows 4 UPST long at 125.74, and moves.json still carries a UPST time stop for 8/11 on a position that closed today. The 8/6 open run inherits both.

The mandate's two arms are both empty and the reason is recorded rather than left as a zero. A closed trade joins an arm through the specification it came from, and neither trade on this board came from one - the AMD round trip pre-dates the mandate entirely, and the UPST round trip has no specification behind it. Attributing either would mean guessing which arm a decision belonged to that was never published, and a miscounted arm is worse than a small one. The mandate was committed at 11:34 ET today, after the 09:42 open run had already fired, so the open slot it binds first is 8/6.

Six scheduled runs and the pre-close all fired inside their windows and all reached the broker - the first full day of that. Every one of them wrote its row. Adherence is unchanged at 1 entry graded and 0 passed, because the only entry the process actually produced this week is still the 8/4 AMD one; today's entry produced no reasoning to grade. Exits stay 1 of 1 for the same reason - the 15:38 sell hit no level (stop 28.60, target 37.31, time stop 8/11, none touched) and came from no run, so counting it as an exit taken on time would credit the process with a decision it did not make and in fact argued against one minute earlier, and counting it as an exit missed would penalise the process for a decision that was not its to make.

bench.json got no row for 8/5. The official settled closes for SPY, QQQ and SMH were still unpublished at 16:37 ET - the broker's close endpoint returns 2026-08-04 for all three, and no 8/5 daily bar exists yet. The 15:59:59 last-trade prints were available and were deliberately not used: this file's own baseline note records that the daily-bar shortcut was stale by 13.66 on SPY, and a last trade written into a column labelled official close is the same failure with a different source. The row is missing rather than approximate. The next retro appends 8/5 before 8/6; baseline is untouched, as always.

Drift check, standing item. docs/RULES.md was edited four times today and every edit was read. One is a loosening and it is the logged one: the daily entry mandate, operator-decided, dated in the rulebook, and named there as a loosening that follows a win. The other three all move the opposite way - an option specification must now carry the broker's own contract id, its label must agree with the chain fields it sits beside, and a specification the account cannot pay for is rejected outright. No exit, stop, sizing, concentration or checklist value has been relaxed, and the +20% / -8% / -40% / five-session table is unchanged. Nothing loosened quietly, and nothing loosened after today, which was a loss.

Drift check, second half: how a number is measured, not only what the rules say. The mandate's labelling requirement is the thing that would decay silently, because a forced entry published unmarked would look exactly like a patient one. It cannot have decayed yet - no specification has been published under the mandate at all, so there is nothing marked or unmarked to inspect, and both arms are legitimately empty rather than quietly miscounted. Recording that plainly matters, because an untested mandate and a perfectly honoured one produce the same zeros. The measurement change this retro did make is in the other direction: totalTrades went from 1 to 2 and losses from 0 to 1 on a day the account lost money, and the loss was taken into the record by the same run that would have benefited from leaving it out.

NO CONNECTOR. This run fired at 16:34 ET against its 16:30 slot and could not reach the brokerage at all - no broker tool was present in its tool set, confirmed twice by direct search and once against the installed-connector list, which returned nothing. This is a connection failure and not a decline: the mandate was set and matched, the slot was in window, and the run attempted the work rather than stopping at a guard. Its row is written with connected=false and counts against run health, which is the point of writing it. Every number in this file is therefore UNCHANGED and unreconciled. totalTrades stays 2, agentTrades 0, the equity curve has no 8/6 point, and no closed trade was added, because the only honest source for any of those is the API and this run had none. It must not be read as a day on which nothing happened.

What could not be established, listed rather than glossed. The account's closing state is unknown to this run. The pre-close read it at 15:36 ET and reported one position held - 2 SMR 8/14 9.50 calls at a 0.57 average - and that is the last verified read in the record, taken twenty-four minutes before the bell. It is not evidence of the close. On 8/5 a fill landed 84 seconds after the equivalent read, which is exactly why a 15:36 read cannot be promoted to a 16:00 fact. So: no fill was confirmed, no position was confirmed still open, no exit was scored, and adherence is untouched at 1 entry graded, 0 passed, 1 exit of 1 on time. The exit question this session actually raises - the final-week rule came due and no exit was published - is left unscored for the same reason, since whether the operator closed the position in the last twenty-four minutes decides it and this run cannot see.

bench.json got no row again, and now two are missing: 8/5 and 8/6. The 8/5 row was owed by this run under the previous retro's own commitment to append it before 8/6. Both were blocked by the same thing - the official settled closes for SPY, QQQ and SMH come from the broker's close endpoint and there was no broker. The alternative was to write something else into a column labelled official close, and this file's baseline note already records why that is not an alternative: the interpolated daily bar was stale by 13.66 on SPY. Missing is the correct rendering of a number that was not obtained. baseline is untouched, as always, and the next connected retro owes three rows rather than one.

ATTRIBUTION. One fill is recorded in the log today and it did not change the autonomy number. The 09:41 open run published the first specification under the daily entry mandate - buy 12 SMR at a 9.75 limit, marked forced on item 1 - and the 10:21 hourly reported that the broker returned no order against it in any state. It expired unexecuted at 10:35. What the account actually bought was different: 2 SMR 8/14 9.50 calls at a 0.57 average, filled 10:46:51 in two legs at 0.55 and 0.59, placed_agent 'user', re-derived from the broker's own order record by the 12:23 run rather than inherited from this log. It is filed 'assisted' and this retro affirms that rather than re-scoring it. The agent supplied the underlying and the published reasoning that picked it over three alternatives; the operator supplied the instrument, strike, expiry and size and pressed the button. Not 'directed' - no agent placed it. Not 'hand' - the name and the case for it came off this board. Not 'agent', and the test was applied rather than assumed: filing it 'agent' would need a published specification matching instrument, side and limit, and the only specification published today was for 12 shares of equity at 9.75, which is not this order. agentTrades stays 0. Fourth consecutive session in which the account traded and the autonomy number did not move.

THE MANDATE'S ARMS ARE STILL BOTH EMPTY, and the reason changed today. A closed trade joins an arm through the specification it came from. The mandate's first binding open slot was 8/6 and the open run discharged it, correctly marked forced with item 1 named and the reason stated - so the mandate is no longer untested. But the specification produced no position: it went unexecuted and expired. The option position that does exist came from no specification, so it belongs to neither arm even if it closes, and it is not closed as far as this run can verify. forced stays 0/0/0 and 0/0/0. The distinction worth keeping is that on 8/5 the arms were empty because nothing had been published; today they are empty because what was published was not taken. Those are different facts about the process and collapsing them into the same zeros would lose the more useful one.

THE GATE CANNOT PUBLISH AN OPTION EXIT. Escalated by the 15:21 and 15:36 runs and verified here from source rather than accepted on report, because it is the most consequential finding on the board and it arrived from the runs it inconveniences. scripts/validate.mjs opens its option block at `if (o.kind === "option")` with no test of action, so the 21-day expiry floor refuses a sell-to-close on a 7-day contract for being too short-dated to buy - the rule the exit exists to honour is the rule that blocks it. The affordability check computes limit x qty x 100 against deployable cash, again with no test of action, so a sell that raises about 98 is refused for costing about 98 against 11.98. Both confirmed by reading the code. One thing neither run had: roughly forty lines above the option block the same file already branches on action - `const buy = o.action === "buy"` - to require a sell's target below its limit rather than above it. The author distinguished buys from sells at the one place the arithmetic reverses and did not carry it into the two places where it also reverses, which makes this an oversight rather than a policy. A third, smaller item for the operator while the file is open: a sell-to-close must still supply target and stop as positive numbers, which have no meaning when closing a position - it does not fail, but it obliges a run to invent two numbers. Not fixed here. The mandate forbids weakening the validator and the drift policy reserves rule changes to the operator, and the case for an agent making this one itself is strong enough to be exactly the case where the gate should hold. The consequence is on the board: the position went into the overnight in breach of the final-week rule from the 8/7 open, held because the exit had no publishable form rather than because the hold was judged better.

THE PRE-CLOSE PUBLISH GAP WAS NOT REMEDIATED AND IS WIDER. The 8/5 retro flagged this slot for a write-then-push with no re-read between them, after the 15:37 read went live as an overnight hold of a position sold at 15:38:23. Today: account read 15:36, state.json stamped 15:36 with a closingNote asserting 'This is the last read of the session', moves.json pruned 15:41, commit at 15:42:13. Six minutes thirteen seconds against three minutes fifty on 8/5, still with no re-read, and now carrying an explicit claim of finality about twenty-four minutes of session the run could not see. The flag was raised, the reasoning it applied to was excellent both days, and the mechanical fix - re-read the account immediately before pushing, or drop the finality claim - was not made. Whether anything filled inside today's window is unknown, because this retro had no connector; that is the compounding, not an exoneration. This is the one process defect on the board that has now been named twice.

CHECKLIST CONTRADICTIONS ON THE OPERATOR'S POSITION, both inside a single session. The 10:46 entry recording the fill marks item 6 pass, but the target, stop and time stop for that position were derived by that entry after the 10:46:51 fill - the exact asterisk the 8/5 retro attached to the 14:21 UPST entry, one day earlier, with an explicit warning that later entries marking item 6 pass on such a position inherit it. All five hourlies that followed marked item 6 fail on the same position, so the entry that recorded the fill is the only one of six reading it as satisfied. Separately, the same entry marks item 1 pass on a catalyst the 09:47 entry had marked fail that morning, on the same name and the same print, with a stated argument that nothing between the two entries answered - and it moves in the direction that makes the operator's fill read better on the rulebook than the board's own specification on the same underlying. Neither changes what happened. Both make the record disagree with itself, which is the rulebook's unlogged-check failure arriving from its other end: a check logged as passed that was not re-run. Flagged, not edited - why.json is immutable and the grades on those entries carry it.

TWO DATE DISAGREEMENTS IN THE RECORD, small and worth fixing before they act on something. First: the open run's runs.json note describes its own specification as carrying 'time stop the 8/13 close', while the specification in why.json - the gated artefact, and the one a person would execute - says '5 sessions - 8/12 close', as does that entry's body. why.json is right; five sessions from 8/6 are 8/6, 8/7, 8/10, 8/11 and 8/12. Second, and live: the option position's time stop is stated as 8/13 in state.json, moves.json and all six hourlies, every one of them in the phrase 'the time stop is 8/13 with today session one of five' - but 8/13 is session six on that count, and the 10:46 entry suggests the date was actually chosen as one day before expiry rather than by counting sessions. So two specifications written the same morning under the same rule produced different dates from the same five-session phrase. The retro does not own runs.json rows written by other runs, state.json or moves.json, so this is flagged for the trading runs rather than edited.

DRIFT CHECK, standing item. docs/RULES.md is unchanged since 8/5 - no edit today, and no exit, stop, sizing, concentration or checklist value has moved. The +20% / -8% / -40% / five-session table stands. The daily entry mandate, the logged 8/5 loosening, had its first binding day today and its labelling requirement was honoured: the entry it produced was published marked forced, with forcedItems naming item 1, a forcedReason stating the failure, and the checklist showing item 1 fail. That is the specific decay this check exists to catch - a forced entry published unmarked would look exactly like a patient one - and it did not occur on the first day it could have. Second half, how a number is measured rather than what the rules say. The pressure today ran the other way and is worth naming: a structural gap was found in the gate by the two runs it blocked, on the last day either could act, and neither amended it. An agent loosening a rule it has just been stopped by, and calling it a correction, is the precise shape of the drift the policy forbids, and the fact that the fix is probably right is what makes the restraint worth crediting rather than what makes it unnecessary. Nothing in this file moved in a flattering direction today, because nothing in it moved at all - adherence, both arms and the trade counts are untouched for want of a connector, not for want of a favourable read. One thing this retro chose not to do, recorded so it is a decision rather than an omission: the 09:47 forced specification is the day's central artefact and it is a 'will' entry, and the retro's authority is to add a grade only to a 'did' entry. It is therefore the first entry ever published under the mandate and it stands ungraded. The mandate created a class of artefact the retro is not permitted to grade, and that is for the operator to resolve rather than for this run to resolve in its own favour.

RECORD-HONESTY CHECKS. runs.json scheduler.configured stays true with its note accurate and narrow - a desktop scheduled task that fires only while the app is open, not a server-side runner. Today supports that reading rather than straining it: eight scheduled rows before this one, all inside their windows, three to eight minutes late. This retro's own row is the day's failure, and it is a connector failure rather than a trigger failure - the trigger fired on time. The position sync is correctly absent from run health: it writes state.json and deliberately writes no runs.json row, and it is not one of the four slots. state.json's lastRefreshUtc is 19:36:00Z, matching the 15:36 pre-close read and unchanged since, so the sync has not written after the pre-close - consistent with a sync that runs in market hours, and stated as an observation rather than a fault. moves.json is clean: the pre-close pruned the 8/5 earnings cluster and the stale UPST 8/11 clock the last retro flagged, re-read every surviving spot from a live bid, and no catalyst with a passed date remains. No account identifier appears anywhere in this repo or in this run's commit.

CONNECTED, and the backlog the 8/6 retro could not touch is cleared. This run fired 16:33 ET against its 16:30 slot and reached the brokerage; the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly and every other account was discarded unread. The SMR round trip is reconciled against the API rather than the log and closes from three directions. Bought 2 SMR 8/14 9.50 calls 10:46:51 ET on 8/6 in two executions at 0.55 and 0.59, processed premium 114.00, placed_agent 'user'. Sold 2 at 0.49 on a 0.48 limit at 15:38:06 ET on 8/6, processed premium 98.00, direction credit, closing_strategy long_call, settlement 8/7. P/L -16.00, -14.04%, held 4h 51m. The broker's own realized-P/L endpoint independently returns -16 on one closing trade for the 8/6 bucket, at a rate of return that rounds to -14.04%, and its per-trade history returns the same -16 against SMR at a 49 close price. Nothing here is reconstructed from P/L arithmetic - every leg came off the order record. The account is FLAT tonight: zero equity positions, zero option positions, 109.88 total, 109.88 buying power, nothing unsettled.

ATTRIBUTION, and the two legs of this trade attribute differently, so both are set down. The row is booked 'assisted' on the opening leg, affirming the 8/6 retro rather than re-scoring it: placed_agent 'user', the agent supplied the underlying and the published reasoning that picked it over four alternatives, the operator supplied the instrument, strike, expiry and size and pressed the button. The CLOSING leg is the one that needs the test applied rather than the broker flag read. It reports placed_agent 'agentic'. Filing it 'agent' requires a published specification in why.json matching instrument, side and limit, plus a scheduled run row lining up with it. There is no such specification and there provably cannot be one: the 15:21 and 15:36 runs on 8/6 both established, and this retro verified from source, that scripts/validate.mjs cannot pass ANY option exit, so no option sell-to-close has ever been publishable in this project. The first test fails outright, so the closing leg is 'directed' at most and is certainly not 'agent'. Either way agentTrades stays 0. Fifth consecutive session in which this account traded or held and the autonomy number did not move.

THE SCOPE ESCALATION, and it is now a pattern rather than an incident. The mandate sets allowOrderPlacement false and no run in this project has order authority. The broker nonetheless reports THREE filled orders in this account with placed_agent 'agentic', and this retro enumerated them by querying that flag directly rather than inferring: the UPST buy at 13:34:59 ET on 8/5, the UPST sell at 15:38:23 ET on 8/5, and the SMR sell at 15:38:05 ET on 8/6. None of the three has a published order specification behind it. Two of the three landed at 15:38 and change, roughly two minutes after that day's pre-close run had read the account - the 8/5 one 84 seconds after, the 8/6 one about two minutes after. The board cannot answer from its own data what placed them, and it must not guess. Recorded as the standing escalation the 8/7 open run raised, with the enumeration attached so the operator has the full set rather than the one instance. This is not an agent in this project loosening a rule; it is a write path into a read-only account that the record cannot account for, which is the more serious of the two.

THE MANDATE'S ARMS ARE STILL BOTH EMPTY, and today is the first time a trade has CLOSED in the mandate era, so the arms were genuinely tested and still take nothing. A closed trade joins an arm through the specification it came from. The SMR option round trip came from no specification: the only thing published on 8/6 was a forced spec for 12 SMR shares at a 9.75 limit, which is a different instrument and a different size, and the broker confirms zero equity orders in this account on or after 8/6, so that spec was never executed at all. Attributing the option trade to the forced arm on the strength of a shared ticker would be the miscount the validator's arm checks exist to prevent, and a miscounted arm is worse than an empty one. forced stays 0/0/0 and 0/0/0. The distinction across three days is worth keeping rather than collapsing: 8/5 empty because nothing was published, 8/6 empty because what was published was not taken, 8/7 empty because nothing was published at all - the open slot fired 143 minutes late and the staleness guard outranked the mandate.

ADHERENCE UNCHANGED at 1 entry graded, 0 passed, 1 exit of 1 on time, and the reasoning is recorded because the temptation this session was to move both numbers in the flattering direction. On entries: the SMR option purchase is not an entry the process produced - the process produced a 12-share equity specification that went unexecuted, and counting the operator's instrument choice as a process entry would attribute the operator's decision to the board, which is the attribution discipline this file rests on running backwards. The 09:47 forced specification is a 'will' entry and the retro's authority is to grade 'did' entries only, so it stays ungraded for a second day; that limitation is the operator's to resolve and not this run's to resolve in its own favour. On exits: the 8/6 exit is NOT counted, and this is the closer call. The process did decide it - five hourlies handed the expiry item forward and the pre-close decided the exit was due on the final-week rule, an entry graded PASS on its own merits - and the fill did land inside the window the rule required. But the process did not place it, no gated specification stands behind it, and the order that filled came from the unexplained agentic path above and was created at 15:38:05, four minutes before the board published its decision at 15:39:18. Crediting the process with an on-time exit executed by an order path the record cannot account for, and which preceded the publication of the decision it supposedly implements, would overstate autonomy in exactly the way this board exists to prevent.
